before: function twice(int $value): int declares an integer parameter and an integer return value. The colon introduces the return type.
Without strict_types, compatible scalar arguments may be converted. Passing numeric string "4" to this int parameter can become integer 4.
An int contract does not establish a permitted score range or that input text followed a specific external format.
Expected output or behavior: 8. Compiler evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.
Optional local transfer task: Separate a type contract from a positive-number or range contract. You may trace it without a PHP interpreter; reading completion is not proof of a local run.
after: A type declaration tells PHP what kind of input a function expects.
The int after the colon says the function gives back a whole number.
This parameter expects an integer. Calls from this file can convert suitable numeric text to that type.
The output is `8`. Four fits and the function doubles it.
